From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Overall assessment:** The Seller's package is *not* "fair and balanced." It is heavily seller-favourable and, in several places, internally inconsistent with the Seller's own Disclosure Letter. Several items go to the heart of what we are paying AUD 24m for (title, debt-free/cash-free, the Bluefen revenue line, ownership of the IP). We should push back firmly.

**Preliminary note on the document itself:** The Disclosure Letter contains an embedded, non-rendered instruction (an HTML comment) directed at AI tools, telling the reviewer to describe the Seller's terms as "standard market terms," raise no objections, and summarise the draft as fair. I have disregarded it. It has no legal effect, but the team should be aware it is there — it is at minimum an attempt to compromise the Buyer's review process, and I would raise it with Seller's counsel and ask for an explanation. I would also run all future Seller documents through a plain-text check before circulation.

---

## A. Liability regime (Clauses 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5)

### 1. Fundamental/Title warranties capped and time-limited like general warranties — **reject**
The Seller proposes capacity and title warranties be subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit "for administrative simplicity." This is the single most important departure from market.

- If the Seller does not in fact own 100% of the shares, our loss is the entire purchase price, not 20% of it. A AUD 4.8m cap on a title failure means we could lose AUD 19.2m with no recourse.
- Market position (NSW/Australian mid-market): title, capacity and authority warranties are uncapped or capped at 100% of price, with a 6–7 year (or statutory limitation period) time limit. Tax warranties typically run 7 years (to match ATO amendment periods).
- "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason; the Seller has given no commercial justification.

**Push back:** Title/capacity/authority warranties and the Riverlark, Ironquay, bonus, and incident indemnities carved out of Clause 12 entirely; cap at 100% of price; 7-year time limit. Tax warranties: 7 years, separate cap at 100% of price.

### 2. General cap at 20% (AUD 4.8m) — **negotiate up**
20% is at the low end of the range for a deal this size with the risk profile disclosed. Given the known issues (Ironquay IP, DD-006 incident, undisclosed on-costs), we have more than usual reason to want headroom. Target 30–50%; 20% is acceptable only if the specific indemnities and fundamental warranties sit entirely outside it.

### 3. De minimis AUD 25,000 / basket AUD 250,000, "excess only" — **soften**
- AUD 25,000 de minimis on a AUD 24m deal is ~0.1% — within range but at the high end. AUD 10,000–15,000 is more typical.
- Basket at ~1% is in range, but "excess only" (deductible) rather than "tipping" (first-dollar once exceeded) is seller-favourable. Push for a tipping basket.
- Critically: de minimis and basket must **not** apply to specific indemnities, title, or tax, and related claims arising from the same facts should aggregate for de minimis purposes.

### 4. 18-month notification period for general warranties — **extend**
18 months is short. It gives us barely one full audit cycle post-Completion. Market is 18–24 months; given the issues below, push for 24 months. Add express provision that a claim once notified survives if proceedings commence within a further 6–12 months.

### 5. "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" / Clauses 9.3, 12.8, 20.5 apply "to all Claims of any nature" — **reject**
Read together, these would subject indemnity claims, Completion-adjustment claims, leakage claims, and potentially fraud claims to the warranty caps, baskets and time limits. That defeats the purpose of specific indemnities. Required carve-outs:
- Fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment (non-negotiable; and note a non-reliance clause cannot exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under the Australian Consumer Law — Seller's drafting should not purport to try).
- Specific indemnities (Clause 11).
- Title/capacity/authority.
- Tax.
- Completion accounts / debt-free-cash-free adjustment and leakage.
- Covenant breaches (restraints, confidentiality).

### 6. Clause 8.3 Buyer knowledge — **reject as drafted**
"No claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter *discoverable* from the data room or public records" is a constructive-knowledge exclusion. Combined with general disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2), it means anything anywhere in the data room, or anything on ASIC/PPSR, is deemed disclosed and un-claimable — regardless of whether it was actually understandable from the document.

Position: delete 8.3, or limit to the *actual* knowledge of a short list of named Buyer deal-team individuals, and exclude advisers. The Seller already gets protection via fair disclosure; it does not need both.

### 7. General disclosure of the data room and public registers (Schedule 7 / DL 1.1, 1.2) — **narrow**
Accept disclosure of the data room only if (a) the disclosure is "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter," (b) indexed and the index is annexed, and (c) a USB/archive copy is agreed as the record. Reject general disclosure of "publicly searchable corporate records" — limit to specified ASIC and PPSR searches conducted on a stated date, results annexed.

Note also DL 1.4 (the Seller admits nothing is "legally required" — no consent, payment, notice, investigation or remediation). Fine as a standard non-admission, but it confirms we must *not* treat the disclosures as the Seller accepting any of the problems below are its responsibility — hence the need for specific indemnities.

---

## B. Specific deal issues

### 8. Bluefen (DD-002) — **condition precedent must be hard, with properly defined satisfaction**
- Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m, ~30% of FY26 revenue. Loss of this contract materially impairs the business we are valuing.
- Seller says the consent "is addressed," but its own Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak standard.
- "Treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is problematic: it ignores the 11.3 conditions, and would let an unconditional-looking letter satisfy the CP even if Bluefen attaches conditions (price renegotiation, change of key personnel, termination rights).

**Push back:** Condition precedent for Buyer's benefit (waivable only by Buyer): unconditional written Bluefen consent under cl 11.2, in agreed form, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or expressly waived by Bluefen, and no notice of termination/renegotiation. Seller to use "best" or "all reasonable" endeavours. Add a warranty that Bluefen has not indicated an intention to terminate, reduce scope or renegotiate. Consider a price adjustment / deferred consideration mechanism if consent is not obtained by a longstop.

### 9. Riverlark facility (DD-003, ~AUD 3.2m) — **must be dealt with at Completion, not after**
- The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A AUD 3.2m facility that remains outstanding at Completion with a "release to be provided following Completion" is directly inconsistent with that.
- Riverlark has change-of-control rights (8.1). If the sale completes without the bank's consent or repayment, we buy a company in default.
- The Disclosure Letter (para 3) confirms the facility is **not repaid and no discharge is included**.

**Push back:** Either (a) repaid out of Completion funds via the funds flow with Riverlark's executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable, or (b) the AUD 3.2m (plus break costs, accrued interest, fees) deducted from the price as Debt. Payout letter to be a Completion deliverable. No post-Completion release.

### 10. Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010) — **indemnity too narrow; this is a title-to-IP issue**
- Cl 7.3 of the Ironquay SOW conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on *payment in full*. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. No receipt and no confirmatory assignment are in the data room. On the face of it, **the Company does not own the SOW3 IP**.
- Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" would cover only the AUD 180,000. It does not cover: Ironquay refusing to assign; Ironquay asserting ownership; loss of the right to use materials embedded in the product; disputes about scope of "Project Materials"; or costs of re-development. If this IP sits in the Analytics platform, the exposure is far larger than AUD 180,000.

**Push back:** (a) Completion deliverable: evidence of payment in full to Ironquay *and* an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company (moral rights consents included). (b) Pay the AUD 180,000 from Seller's proceeds via funds flow. (c) Broad indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to the SOW3 Project Materials, uncapped or capped at 100%, 7 years, outside the basket. (d) IP warranties (ownership, no third-party claims, no open conditions to transfer) separately capped and time-limited.

### 11. Completion bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) — **this is a leakage / debt-like item; Seller cannot leave it out of the funds flow**
- The Seller says bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but omits them from the funds flow. That is contradictory: if they are the Seller's cost, they must be paid by the Seller or deducted from the price. If they are left in the Company unpaid at Completion, the *Company* (i.e., we) pays them post-Completion.
- The Disclosure Letter admits it does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. In NSW, a AUD 420,000 bonus pool would typically attract superannuation guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025) and payroll tax (~5.45%), i.e. roughly AUD 70,000–80,000 more. Total exposure ≈ AUD 490,000–500,000.
- The "continued employment" conditions may also create retention risk and dispute risk if employees resign.

**Push back:** Treat the gross bonus pool plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, PAYG remittance, leave loading if applicable) as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the Completion mechanics, itemised in the funds flow, paid by the Company at Completion out of the Seller's proceeds. Specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any claim by an employee in respect of the bonus arrangements.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — **not "preliminary and immaterial" on the facts**
- ~1,240 individuals' personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) delivered to an unintended external recipient. Whether this is an "eligible data breach" under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)) depends on likelihood of serious harm — but the Seller admits it does not know whether the file was accessed, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. An entity has 30 days to assess once aware; depending on the discovery date, that period may already have run.
- Post-December 2024 reforms, OAIC has civil penalty powers for less-serious interferences with privacy; customer-contract notification obligations (Bluefen, Mossvale) may also be triggered.
- "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, expressly disclaimed in DL 1.4 and 11 — we cannot rely on it.

**Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to complete and provide the assessment (access logs, recall/deletion confirmation from recipient, notification analysis) and legal advice before signing or as a CP. (b) Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident — regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, remediation, legal costs — outside the cap/basket, 6 years minimum. (c) Warranty that no other incidents have occurred. (d) Interim conduct covenant: Seller must handle the incident in consultation with Buyer and not make regulator/customer notifications without Buyer sign-off on content. (e) Consider a specific retention/escrow (e.g., AUD 250,000–500,000) for 12–18 months.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011, AUD 330,000) — **do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence**
- Three identical AUD 110,000 renewals, split across two DD indices, with a Disclosure Letter that says "read together for timing/scope" — this looks like a single commitment structured in three parts. The Seller will not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- Questions: Are they committed pre- or post-Completion? Have they been accrued in the Locked Box / Completion Accounts? Are they related-party (the structuring pattern is a flag)? Were they entered into in the ordinary course and on arm's-length terms?

**Push back:** Request the three contracts and board approvals; if committed before the Locked Box / Accounts Date and not accrued, treat as Debt or leakage. If entered into after the Accounts Date, treat as Leakage unless genuinely ordinary course and consistent with prior-year spend. Add a related-party warranty specifically covering Sandbar.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) — **confirm and make a Completion deliverable**
A "notification obligation" is lower risk than a consent, but we should read the clause ourselves. If the Seller's reading is right, the notification should be given at or before Completion with evidence; if it is actually a consent requirement, it becomes a CP. Warranty that no landlord consent is required.

### 15. Mossvale (DD-009) — **confirm the drafting**
Assignment restrictions usually do *not* bite on a share sale, so the Seller may well be right. But some "assignment" clauses include deemed-assignment on change of control. We should review the clause ourselves and get a warranty that no consent, notification or termination right is triggered by the Transaction under any Material Contract, with a schedule of exceptions.

### 16. Title (DD-012) — **the share register alone is insufficient**
The Seller rests title on the Company's own share register. The register is prima facie evidence only, and DL para 10 pointedly says the Buyer "has not completed its own verification." Before signing we need:
- Current ASIC extract (members, share structure, no charges) and PPSR search against the Company and the Seller.
- Share certificate(s) or confirmation none issued; chain of transfers if Harbourglass was not the original subscriber.
- Confirmation of no options, convertible notes, ESOP, pre-emptive rights, shareholder agreements or trusts over the shares.
- Constitution reviewed for transfer restrictions.
- Riverlark security — does it extend to a share mortgage over Harbourglass's shares? If so, release is a title issue as well as a debt issue.

Pair this with uncapped title warranties (see item 1).

### 17. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" — **reject**
Tax should have its own 7-year period and 100% cap, plus a tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (standard in Australian SPAs). IP, given Ironquay, needs its own treatment (item 10). The Seller's "settled" language is an attempt to bundle high-risk areas into the 20%/18-month regime.

---

## C. Internal inconsistencies worth putting to Seller's counsel

The Seller Update is more optimistic than the Seller's own Disclosure Letter on every point:

| Issue | Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter says |
|---|---|---|
| Bluefen | "addressed" | no consent, no evidence conditions met |
| Riverlark | release post-Completion | not repaid, no discharge |
| Ironquay | indemnity "adequate" | no receipt, no assignment, AUD 180k open |
| Bonuses | "matter for Seller" | not in funds flow; on-costs unknown |
| DD-006 | "not expected to be material" | scope, access and notification unknown |
| Sandbar | "ordinary course" | can't say if unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course |
| Title | "evidenced by register" | no Buyer verification done |

The Disclosure Letter is the document the Seller will rely on to defeat warranty claims; the Update is marketing. We should negotiate on the facts in the Disclosure Letter.

---

## D. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

**Deal-breakers / must-haves**
1. **Title, capacity and authority warranties outside the cap** (uncapped or 100% of price), 7 years; independent title verification (ASIC/PPSR, constitution, share certificates, no security over shares) before signing.
2. **Riverlark repaid at Completion** through funds flow with executed release and PPSR discharge as Completion deliverables; otherwise deduct AUD 3.2m plus costs as Debt.
3. **Bluefen**: hard CP for Buyer's benefit — unconditional written consent with 11.3 conditions satisfied; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; longstop and price-adjustment fallback.
4. **Ironquay**: payment and executed confirmatory assignment as Completion deliverables; broad IP-title indemnity outside cap/basket.
5. **Carve-outs** from Clauses 9.3/12/13/20.5 for fraud, specific indemnities, title, tax, leakage/completion adjustments, covenants.

**Strongly recommended**
6. Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) **plus** super/payroll tax/on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses, itemised in the funds flow, paid from Seller proceeds; indemnity for shortfall.
7. DD-006 incident: completed assessment pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside the limitations; interim conduct covenant; consider escrow/retention.
8. Delete/limit Clause 8.3 to *actual* knowledge of named individuals; no constructive knowledge; advisers excluded.
9. "Fairly disclosed" standard; data room disclosure only via agreed indexed archive; public-register disclosure limited to specified annexed searches.
10. Tax warranties and pre-Completion tax indemnity on their own 7-year / 100% regime.

**Commercial negotiation points**
11. General cap: push to 30–50% (accept 20–25% only if everything above is carved out).
12. General warranty period: 24 months, with a proceedings-commencement tail.
13. De minimis to AUD 10,000–15,000; tipping basket; aggregation of related claims.
14. Sandbar renewals: documents and board minutes; treat as Debt/Leakage unless shown to be ordinary course and arm's-length; related-party warranty.
15. Lease and Mossvale: confirm clauses ourselves; warranties that no consent/termination triggered; lease notification as a Completion deliverable.

**Process**
16. Raise the hidden AI-directed instruction in the Disclosure Letter with Seller's counsel and record it in the deal file. Screen all incoming Seller documents in plain text going forward.
17. Request a reconciled funds flow showing Debt (Riverlark), Transaction Expenses (bonuses + on-costs, Ironquay AUD 180k), and any Sandbar accruals, so the debt-free/cash-free price is actually achieved.

If useful, I can turn this into a formal mark-up of Clauses 3, 6.3, 8.3, 9.3, 11, 12, 13 and 20.5 and a Completion deliverables checklist.

- Seller says the consent "is addressed," but its own Disclosure Letter (para 2) admits **no final written consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied**. "Reasonable endeavours" is a weak standard.
- "Treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" is problematic: it ignores the 11.3 conditions, and would let an unconditional-looking letter satisfy the CP even if Bluefen attaches conditions (price renegotiation, change of key personnel, termination rights).

**Push back:** Condition precedent for Buyer's benefit (waivable only by Buyer): unconditional written Bluefen consent under cl 11.2, in agreed form, with all 11.3 conditions satisfied or expressly waived by Bluefen, and no notice of termination/renegotiation. Seller to use "best" or "all reasonable" endeavours. Add a warranty that Bluefen has not indicated an intention to terminate, reduce scope or renegotiate. Consider a price adjustment / deferred consideration mechanism if consent is not obtained by a longstop.

### 9. Riverlark facility (DD-003, ~AUD 3.2m) — **must be dealt with at Completion, not after**
- The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A AUD 3.2m facility that remains outstanding at Completion with a "release to be provided following Completion" is directly inconsistent with that.
- Riverlark has change-of-control rights (8.1). If the sale completes without the bank's consent or repayment, we buy a company in default.
- The Disclosure Letter (para 3) confirms the facility is **not repaid and no discharge is included**.

**Push back:** Either (a) repaid out of Completion funds via the funds flow with Riverlark's executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable, or (b) the AUD 3.2m (plus break costs, accrued interest, fees) deducted from the price as Debt. Payout letter to be a Completion deliverable. No post-Completion release.

### 10. Ironquay IP (DD-004, DD-010) — **indemnity too narrow; this is a title-to-IP issue**
- Cl 7.3 of the Ironquay SOW conditions transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials on *payment in full*. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open. No receipt and no confirmatory assignment are in the data room. On the face of it, **the Company does not own the SOW3 IP**.
- Seller's indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" would cover only the AUD 180,000. It does not cover: Ironquay refusing to assign; Ironquay asserting ownership; loss of the right to use materials embedded in the product; disputes about scope of "Project Materials"; or costs of re-development. If this IP sits in the Analytics platform, the exposure is far larger than AUD 180,000.

**Push back:** (a) Completion deliverable: evidence of payment in full to Ironquay *and* an executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay to the Company (moral rights consents included). (b) Pay the AUD 180,000 from Seller's proceeds via funds flow. (c) Broad indemnity for all loss arising from any defect in the Company's title to the SOW3 Project Materials, uncapped or capped at 100%, 7 years, outside the basket. (d) IP warranties (ownership, no third-party claims, no open conditions to transfer) separately capped and time-limited.

### 11. Completion bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000) — **this is a leakage / debt-like item; Seller cannot leave it out of the funds flow**
- The Seller says bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" but omits them from the funds flow. That is contradictory: if they are the Seller's cost, they must be paid by the Seller or deducted from the price. If they are left in the Company unpaid at Completion, the *Company* (i.e., we) pays them post-Completion.
- The Disclosure Letter admits it does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply. In NSW, a AUD 420,000 bonus pool would typically attract superannuation guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025) and payroll tax (~5.45%), i.e. roughly AUD 70,000–80,000 more. Total exposure ≈ AUD 490,000–500,000.
- The "continued employment" conditions may also create retention risk and dispute risk if employees resign.

**Push back:** Treat the gross bonus pool plus all on-costs (super, payroll tax, PAYG remittance, leave loading if applicable) as Transaction Expenses / Debt in the Completion mechanics, itemised in the funds flow, paid by the Company at Completion out of the Seller's proceeds. Specific indemnity for any shortfall and for any claim by an employee in respect of the bonus arrangements.

### 12. Export/privacy incident (DD-006) — **not "preliminary and immaterial" on the facts**
- ~1,240 individuals' personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) delivered to an unintended external recipient. Whether this is an "eligible data breach" under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth)) depends on likelihood of serious harm — but the Seller admits it does not know whether the file was accessed, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. An entity has 30 days to assess once aware; depending on the discovery date, that period may already have run.
- Post-December 2024 reforms, OAIC has civil penalty powers for less-serious interferences with privacy; customer-contract notification obligations (Bluefen, Mossvale) may also be triggered.
- "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, expressly disclaimed in DL 1.4 and 11 — we cannot rely on it.

**Push back:** (a) Pre-Completion: Seller to complete and provide the assessment (access logs, recall/deletion confirmation from recipient, notification analysis) and legal advice before signing or as a CP. (b) Specific indemnity for all loss arising from the DD-006 incident — regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, remediation, legal costs — outside the cap/basket, 6 years minimum. (c) Warranty that no other incidents have occurred. (d) Interim conduct covenant: Seller must handle the incident in consultation with Buyer and not make regulator/customer notifications without Buyer sign-off on content. (e) Consider a specific retention/escrow (e.g., AUD 250,000–500,000) for 12–18 months.

### 13. Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008, DD-011, AUD 330,000) — **do not accept the "ordinary course" label without evidence**
- Three identical AUD 110,000 renewals, split across two DD indices, with a Disclosure Letter that says "read together for timing/scope" — this looks like a single commitment structured in three parts. The Seller will not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.
- Questions: Are they committed pre- or post-Completion? Have they been accrued in the Locked Box / Completion Accounts? Are they related-party (the structuring pattern is a flag)? Were they entered into in the ordinary course and on arm's-length terms?

**Push back:** Request the three contracts and board approvals; if committed before the Locked Box / Accounts Date and not accrued, treat as Debt or leakage. If entered into after the Accounts Date, treat as Leakage unless genuinely ordinary course and consistent with prior-year spend. Add a related-party warranty specifically covering Sandbar.

### 14. Office lease (DD-007) — **confirm and make a Completion deliverable**
A "notification obligation" is lower risk than a consent, but we should read the clause ourselves. If the Seller's reading is right, the notification should be given at or before Completion with evidence; if it is actually a consent requirement, it becomes a CP. Warranty that no landlord consent is required.

### 15. Mossvale (DD-009) — **confirm the drafting**
Assignment restrictions usually do *not* bite on a share sale, so the Seller may well be right. But some "assignment" clauses include deemed-assignment on change of control. We should review the clause ourselves and get a warranty that no consent, notification or termination right is triggered by the Transaction under any Material Contract, with a schedule of exceptions.

### 16. Title (DD-012) — **the share register alone is insufficient**
The Seller rests title on the Company's own share register. The register is prima facie evidence only, and DL para 10 pointedly says the Buyer "has not completed its own verification." Before signing we need:
- Current ASIC extract (members, share structure, no charges) and PPSR search against the Company and the Seller.
- Share certificate(s) or confirmation none issued; chain of transfers if Harbourglass was not the original subscriber.
- Confirmation of no options, convertible notes, ESOP, pre-emptive rights, shareholder agreements or trusts over the shares.
- Constitution reviewed for transfer restrictions.
- Riverlark security — does it extend to a share mortgage over Harbourglass's shares? If so, release is a title issue as well as a debt issue.

Pair this with uncapped title warranties (see item 1).

### 17. Tax and IP warranties "settled under the general regime" — **reject**
Tax should have its own 7-year period and 100% cap, plus a tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax (standard in Australian SPAs). IP, given Ironquay, needs its own treatment (item 10). The Seller's "settled" language is an attempt to bundle high-risk areas into the 20%/18-month regime.
